 Order On Board

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed being aggrieved by the
award dated 11.08.2016 passed by the Fourth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Durg in
Claim Case No. 91/2015.
Neutral Citation 2023:Cghc:23217
2.

Facts of the case in brief is that the appellants/claimants have filed application under under
Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming total compensation of Rs. 89,69,600/- on
account of death of deceased Jagdish Pandey in an unfortunate accident that took place on
28.02.20215.

As per the pleadings of the claim application, on the date of incident at about 9.30 pm.
when the deceased was traveling along with acquainted people on a test drive of Hyundai Verna Car
bearing temporary No. Gj -03/T.C./514 and Gj -03/Tc/513 to Devbhoomi, Dwarka and as they
reached near village Vadatra, respondent No.1 drove the offending vehicle rashly and negligently
and dashed to a nearby tree and caused serious injury to the person of the deceased and he was
taken to Khambalia Hospital, where looking to his serious condition, he was referred to G.G.
Hospital, Jamnagar where during treatment, he died on 21.12.2015. The accident was reported to
the police station Khambalia, District Devbhoomi, Dwarka (Gujrat) upon which Crime No. 28/2015
under Sections 279, 337, 338 and 304-A of the Indian Penal Code 1860 was registered and the
offending vehicle was also seized.

After due investigation charge sheet was filed before the
competent court.

3. Further pleadings in the claim application is that deceased Jagdish Pandey was aged about 44
years at the time of accident and was working in the Nova Iron and Steel Limited, Nova Nagar,
Tahsil Belha, District Bilaspur on the post of Manager.

He was earning about Rs. 36,300/- per
month.

The offending vehicle was driven by respondent No.1/driver owned by respondent No.2 and
insured with the Insurance Company therefore all of them are liable to pay compensation as claimed
and stated above.

4. Respondent No.1 &2/driver and owner of the offending vehicle were proceeded ex parte and did
not file any written statement.

Respondent No.3/Insurance Company filed its written statement and
barring the admitted Neutral Citation 2023:Cghc:23217 fact denied the remaining averments of
the claim application with regard to age, profession, monthly income etc.

It was further pleaded that
the offending vehicle was being used in violation of terms and conditions of the Insurance policy
therefore without any valid permit, fitness and driving license therefore the Insurance Company is
not liable to pay the compensation.
5.
Learned Tribunal framed as many as four issues on the basis of the above broad pleadings.

Issue
with regard to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent No.1/driver
and issue No.2 with regard to violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance policy was
Smt. Archana Pandey vs Ravi Rawal on 19 September, 2023
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42222340/
2

decided in favour of the appellants/claimants.
Issue No.3 and 4

with regard to the relief and cost,
the learned Tribunal was pleased to award Rs. 49,82,900/- as total compensation in favour of the
appellants
/ claimants

. 
6. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the income of the deceased was taken on the
lower side as his income was Rs. 36,300/- whereas the Tribunal has assessed his income to Rs.
32,610/- which is on the lower side.
It is submitted that the
learned Tribunal ought to have awarded more compensation to make the same just and proper.

7. Shri Amrito Das, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company vehemently opposes the submissions and submits that the income of the deceased was proved as Rs. 32,610/- by leading evidence and on the basis of which, the findings so recorded cannot be said to be perverse or contrary to the record.
He further submits that though 30% future prospect is awarded on the income of the deceased but under other heads sufficient amount has been awarded therefore it does not require any interference.

8. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the records.
9.

The claimants have pleaded that the income of the deceased was Rs. 36,300/- but the evidence which has been brought on record clearly Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:23217 establishes that after necessary deduction, his monthly income has been assessed to Rs. 32,610/-.

The findings recorded by the learned Tribunal appears to have been based upon proper appreciation of evidence brought on record therefore such finding cannot be said to be in the opinion of the court perverse or contrary to the records.
Apart from this, the Tribunal has also added 30% as future prospects on he income of the deceased.

On the other hand, the Tribunal has also awarded Rs. 25,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs. 50,000/- towards love and affection, Rs. 1,00,000/- for loss of consortium and Rs.
55,000/- has been awarded towards traveling expenses and Rs. 4,800/- towards staying in the Dharamshala.
Thus, in view of the foregoing discussion, the findings so recorded does not appear to be illegal and perverse.
10. In the result, the appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

Sd/-
(Sachin Singh Rajput) Judge suguna Smt. Archana Pandey vs Ravi Rawal on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42222340/
